To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the hierarchical three-dimensional multiscale electro–magneto–thermal model of quenching in $\text{REBa}_{\text{2}}\text{Cu}_{\text{3}}\text{O}_{\text{7}-\delta }$ (REBCO)-coated-conductor-based coils can be used to study the quench behavior at multiple length scales, from the microscale to the macroscale.

a) the hierarchical multiscale approach can be used to model quench behavior of REBCO CC-based coils; b) the approach is validated by comparing simulation and experimental results; and c) the results show that the quench behavior in the coil is sensitive to the quench location, quench current, and coil configuration, and the quench behavior can be predicted using the multiscale approach.

(1) the proposed hierarchical three-dimensional multiscale electro-magneto thermal coil quench model can accurately predict the electrical, magnetic and thermal behavior of REBCO CC based coils; (2) quench behavior of REBCOC based coils is highly non-uniform; (3) quench detection and quench protection methods must be designed based on the quench behavior of the coil at the location where quench detection and/or quench protection is desired.

the development of a multiscale quench model of REBCO CCs.
developing a modular 3D electro-magneto thermal coil quench model that can be used for the design and analysis of quench protection methods and coil reliability.
the development of a hierarchical multiscale electro-magneto–thermal model of quenching in REBCO CC-based coils and the validation of the model through comparison with experiment.

this hierarchical multiscale electro-magneto thermal coil quench model can be used for the study of quench behavior of REBCO CC-based superconducting magnets and coils at multiple length scales.
